proposed_widenings.name: level_up_grant family for ClassFeatureMechanics
proposed_widenings.justification: Ability Score Improvement is a permanent character-progression benefit granted once at level-up. It has no activation cost, no use-count resource, and no reset cadence — none of the structural fields required by the only existing ClassFeatureFamily ("activation") apply. A new family is needed to encode features that are permanent passive grants made at the moment of leveling up.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_feat effect atom
proposed_widenings.justification: The effect of the feature is to grant the player a feat (specifically the Ability Score Improvement feat or another qualifying feat). No existing ClassFeatureEffect covers feat grants. The v4 taxonomy notes modify_ability_score is currently out-of-scope, and grant_proficiency covers a different concept.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat (see "Feats") or another feat of your choice for which you qualify.

notes: This is the standard level-4 ASI feature shared across all classes. The structural gap is class-feature-family level: ClassFeatureMechanics only supports 'activation', which models activatable in-play abilities with resources and reset cadences. ASI is a one-time level-up benefit — a completely different shape. The v4 taxonomy explicitly calls modify_ability_score out-of-scope as a runtime effect. All other ASI-at-level-N features across the full class roster (barbarian, bard, cleric, druid, fighter, monk, paladin, ranger, rogue, sorcerer, warlock, wizard) will face the same structural gap.
